section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Average Speed Concept
section_1.content: Recall that average speed is total distance divided by total time. Visually, this is the slope of a secant line connecting two distinct points (P and Q) on a position-time graph.
section_1.example: A cheetah runs 100 meters in 5 seconds. Average speed = 20 m/s. Visually: A straight line connecting the start and end point on the distance curve.

section_2.title: The Problem of 'Instantaneous' Speed
section_2.content: What if we want to know the cheetah's speed at exactly 2 seconds? Our standard formula fails because the time interval becomes zero (division by zero). Introduce the idea of shrinking the interval.
section_2.example: The cheetah's speedometer shows its exact speed at 2.00s. We move point Q closer and closer to point P on the graph.

section_3.title: The Limit Process: Approaching the Tangent
section_3.content: Explain that as the time interval Δt approaches zero, the secant line morphs into a tangent line. The slope of this tangent line represents the instantaneous rate of change.
section_3.example: Animation: Point Q 'slides' along the curve toward P. The secant line tilts until it matches the curve's slope at exactly point P.

section_4.title: Defining the Derivative
section_4.content: Formally define the derivative as the limit of the difference quotient: f'(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. This is the mathematical 'tool' to calculate the instantaneous rate of change.
section_4.example: Applying the formula to a simple function like f(x) = x² to find the general slope at any point x.

section_5.title: Application: Real-world Significance
section_5.content: Summarize that the derivative is not just a math symbol; it is the 'local' behavior of a function. Used in physics (velocity), economics (marginal cost), and biology (growth rates).
section_5.example: A rocket launch: The derivative tells us the exact vertical velocity at any second t, crucial for ensuring the rocket doesn't break under pressure.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.2
